Rules extracted from the applications themselves, not from their documentation.

Each file in this directory records what one installed application accepts, the
version it was read from, and the exact command that read it, so the claim can
be re-checked rather than believed. The rule that makes them load-bearing is
spec section 5 of specs/PR-DESKTOP-APPS-CONFIGURE-SPEC.md: a desktop app keeps
its Configure button only where MCC's generated document is validated in CI
against a rule extracted from that app's own shipped code or published schema.

The precedent is tests/fixtures/schemas/, which vendors OpenCode's and Crush's
own published JSON Schemas. This directory is for the apps that publish none.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
roo-code-3.54.0.json
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
App:        Roo Code (VS Code extension, publisher rooveterinaryinc)
Version:    3.54.0, from its package.json "version"
Read from:  %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions\rooveterinaryinc.roo-cline-3.54.0
Date:       2026-09-12
Platform:   Windows 11, VS Code 1.136.1

Extraction (Git Bash; the bundle is one 14.8 MB minified line, so every read is
a grep for the identifier rather than a line number):

    EXT=~/.vscode/extensions/rooveterinaryinc.roo-cline-3.54.0

    # the settings key the extension reads at activation
    grep -o 'autoImportSettingsPath.\{0,220\}' "$EXT/dist/extension.js"
    grep -o 'roo-cline\.autoImportSettingsPath' "$EXT/package.json"

    # the shape of the document that key names
    grep -o 'providerProfiles:.\{0,160\}globalSettings:.\{0,120\}' "$EXT/dist/extension.js"
    grep -o 'currentApiConfigName:.\{0,200\}' "$EXT/dist/extension.js"

    # the apiProvider enum, in the five parts the bundle splits it into
    grep -o 'Htr=.\{0,700\}' "$EXT/dist/extension.js"
    for v in Qtr Btr uNi cNi dNi; do grep -o "$v=\[[^]]\{0,300\}" "$EXT/dist/extension.js"; done

    # the OpenAI-compatible profile's own keys
    grep -o 'openAiBaseUrl:.\{0,500\}' "$EXT/dist/extension.js"

    # openAiCustomModelInfo, and which of its members are required
    grep -o 'AP=[a-zA-Z0-9_$]*\.object({[^}]\{0,600\}' "$EXT/dist/extension.js"

Not extracted, and so not asserted: what Roo does with the profile *after* the
import. The import itself was not run -- that would write the user's own VS Code
SecretStorage -- so this rule says what the document has to look like to be
accepted, and nothing about what the extension then sends on the wire.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
codex-0.153.4.json
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
App:        Codex desktop (the MSIX ChatGPT app, OpenAI.Codex 26.901.6511.0)
            and the npm CLI. Both unpack the same engine and read the same
            ~/.codex/config.toml.
Version:    codex-cli 0.153.4, from `codex --version`
Read from:  %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\8e5b6932251c2c1c\codex.exe
Date:       2026-09-12 (strings first taken 2026-09-08; re-greped for this rule)
Platform:   Windows 11

Extraction (the binary publishes no schema, so the evidence is its own string
table plus live runs under a scratch CODEX_HOME -- never the user's):

    # the 17-field serde list, emitted beside the struct's name
    grep -oa '.\{0,120\}wire_apiquery_paramshttp_headers.\{0,220\}' codex.strings.txt

    # the wire_api rejection, six occurrences
    grep -oa 'wire_api[ =]\{0,3\}.\{0,90\}' codex.strings.txt | sort -u

    # the credential errors
    grep -oa 'Missing environment variable.\{0,80\}' codex.strings.txt

    # behaviour, against a scratch CODEX_HOME and base_url http://127.0.0.1:1/v1
    CODEX_HOME=<scratch> codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "say hi"
    CODEX_HOME=<scratch> codex doctor

`codex.strings.txt` is `strings -n 6` over that codex.exe (24.8 MB of output).

Not extracted, and so not asserted: what the desktop GUI does *after* a valid
config loads. openai/codex#29156 reports the model picker degrading with any
custom provider; the app was never launched.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
claude-desktop-1.46388.4.0.json
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
App:        Claude Desktop (Microsoft Store / MSIX package)
Version:    1.46388.4.0, from the package directory name
Read from:  C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\Claude_1.46388.4.0_x64__pzs8sxrjxfjjc
            \app\resources\app.asar
Date:       2026-09-12 (extracted 2026-09-08; re-greped for this rule)
Platform:   Windows 11

Extraction:

    npx @electron/asar extract app.asar <scratch>/asar
    npx prettier --parser babel \
        <scratch>/asar/.vite/build/index.chunk--WuAOADe.js \
        > chunk-WuAOADe.pretty.js

    grep -n 'a-f0-9-\]{36}' chunk-WuAOADe.pretty.js      # the entry-id regex
    grep -n 'inferenceProvider' chunk-WuAOADe.pretty.js  # LTe, flatKey, enum
    grep -n 'inferenceCredentialKind' chunk-WuAOADe.pretty.js
    grep -o 'inference[A-Za-z]*' chunk-WuAOADe.pretty.js | sort -u
    sed -n '27975,27995p' chunk-WuAOADe.pretty.js        # ao / oo / Cve
    sed -n '27700,27790p' chunk-WuAOADe.pretty.js        # Ga / Ka / d_e
    sed -n '31860,31890p' chunk-WuAOADe.pretty.js        # BCe, the model filter

The application was **never launched**. Spec section 5 excludes it from
launch-proof by name: it is a packaged Store app signed into a real account.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
goose-1.50.0.json
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
App:        Goose desktop / CLI (Block)
Version:    v1.50.0, the release tag
Read from:  goose-source-v1.50.0.zip, the release's own source archive
Date:       2026-09-12
Platform:   n/a -- source, not a binary. Goose is NOT installed on this
            machine (no goose.exe or goosed.exe on PATH, in Program Files,
            scoop, cargo, go/bin or the uninstall registry), which is why the
            source archive is the artefact. Nothing here was put on the wire.

Extraction (Git Bash):

    gh release download v1.50.0 --repo block/goose \
        --pattern 'goose-source-v1.50.0.zip'
    unzip -o -j goose-source-v1.50.0.zip \
        goose-v1.50.0/crates/goose-providers/src/declarative.rs \
        goose-v1.50.0/crates/goose-providers/src/openai.rs \
        goose-v1.50.0/crates/goose-provider-types/src/base.rs \
        goose-v1.50.0/crates/goose/src/config/declarative_providers.rs \
        goose-v1.50.0/crates/goose-providers/src/declarative/definitions/lmstudio.json \
        -d .

    grep -n 'pub struct DeclarativeProviderConfig' -A 46 declarative.rs
    grep -n 'enum ProviderEngine' -A 20 declarative.rs
    grep -n 'fn load_custom_providers' -A 18 declarative.rs
    grep -n 'fn create_custom_provider' -A 45 declarative_providers.rs
    grep -n 'fn from_declarative_config' -A 50 openai.rs
    grep -n 'pub struct ModelInfo' -A 26 base.rs

Not extracted, and so not asserted: anything about what a running Goose sends.
The rule says what the document has to look like to deserialise and how the
credential is resolved, and nothing about the wire.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
command-code-1.50.0.json
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
App:        Command Code CLI
Version:    1.50.0, from its package.json "version"
Read from:  %APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\command-code\dist\cli.mjs
Date:       2026-09-12
Platform:   Windows 11

Extraction. The bundle is one 2.5 MB minified line, and a windowed grep over
it does not finish, so the reads are a small script that prints a fixed window
around each literal:

    uv run --offline python scan.py dist/cli.mjs 200 "providers.json"
    uv run --offline python scan.py dist/cli.mjs 180 "modelProvider"
    uv run --offline python scan.py dist/cli.mjs 150 "config.json"

(`scan.py` is ten lines: read the file, re.finditer the escaped needle, print
`text[start-width : end+width]`.) The user's own ~/.commandcode was read
read-only and nothing under it was written.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
opencode-1.18.26.json  and  crush-0.92.0.json
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
These two applications publish machine-readable schemas, which
tests/fixtures/schemas/ has vendored since the catalogue-contract work:

    opencode-config.schema.json   from https://opencode.ai/config.json
                                  (OpenCode 1.18.25/1.18.26 loaded the
                                  generated document and reported MCC's
                                  models with MCC's limits)
    crush.schema.json             emitted by the binary itself,
                                  `crush schema` on v0.92.0 -- an
                                  undocumented command, not in --help

So the rule files above do not restate the schema. They record which document
the desktop card's block is embedded in before validation (`embed_at`), and
the handful of behaviours a JSON Schema cannot express -- each of which was
measured on the wire against the running binary at the time, and is quoted
with what was measured.
